With its source gone the old pair could only score Inconclusive forever while presenting as a settled row, so the row now points at a guard on the resolution itself, which fails if a hardcoded size returns.

The old pair compared two particular sentences to each other. On 2026-09-05 the vendor corrected 10 to 11 and consolidated the duplicate, which removes an operand -- the claim would have gone green by losing the thing it compared, which is the failure mode this suite exists to prevent. The replacement reads every stated species count anywhere in llms.txt and settles them all against the live catalogue, so it fails on internal disagreement and on agreed-upon drift alike.

The old check POSTed an empty body and demanded 401/403, reading the 422 as ungated filing. An empty body names no wallet, so there is nothing for an attribution gate to refuse and 422 is the correct answer -- it was failing their design decision, not a defect. Open intake is deliberate: anonymous, per-IP rate limited, 24h duplicate-title gate. Report #47's real subject was that a filing could be attributed to a wallet its author does not control, and they fixed that in d12ea54a9: naming a verified wallet without an EIP-191 signature or an owning session is refused 401 WALLET_SIGNATURE_REQUIRED. The new check asserts that mechanism -- the signing message names the wallet, binds sha256(title) against replay, and is deterministic -- verified live 2026-09-05 without signing anything or filing a probe report.

Ours. The report asserted the credentialed caller was served above its tier, but the tier came from the name of our own config variable (QA_TRUSTED_KEY), not from the platform. GET /mcp/v1/agents/me reports this caller as allied with trust_score 9419, and at that tier the served set is exactly the entitled set: 56 and 56, nothing above. The vendor closed #54 as invalid and was right. Not VERIFIED FIXED, because nothing was broken and nothing was fixed -- the finding should never have been filed. Retracted to them in report #62. text: Resolved two ways, both measured, neither of which the pinned check is allowed to call a pass on its own. Three paths were RENAMED and the successors are served -- /api/v1/account/me answers 401, /api/v1/clob/orders 405, /api/v1/agentbook/posts 200 -- and those three now pass. The other 23 were REMOVED from the documentation rather than fixed in place, which the check deliberately scores Inconclusive because withdrawing a promise is the vendor's call to announce, not ours to bank for them. They did announce it, per path and with causes, in the closing note on #49: backtest/run, backtest/saved, defi/pools, the /mcp/v1/prompts/* entries (the JSON-RPC server implements no prompts methods) and the GET-able /mcp/v1/tools and /mcp/v1/resources link rendering were deleted as never-built. So the row reads NOT REPRODUCIBLE, and the honest reading of that is 'resolved, but 23 of 26 by deletion rather than by building' -- not 'our check is broken'. Left open deliberately: if any of those 23 paths returns to the documentation while still 404, the pin catches it.

Reports #49 and #59 document the original failure: 26 paths promised by llms.txt and agent-skills.json answered 404. The check definition changed twice on 2026-09-05, both times to stop it lying. First, path matching became boundary-aware -- it had compared paths as substrings, so /api/v1/account matched inside /api/v1/account/me and three renames the vendor shipped on 09-04 kept reading as unfixed, which is what report #59 was chasing. Second, a path deleted from the documentation now passes rather than scoring Inconclusive: the defect was that the docs promised what the server did not serve, and deletion resolves it, with the reason line saying it was resolved by deletion rather than by building. All 26 pins stay named here forever, so nothing can be hidden by removing it. Result under the new definition: 3 renamed and their successors served (verified by calling them), 23 removed from the documentation, 0 still promised and broken.

reason: The check definition moved on 2026-09-06 and the platform did not. It read the species catalogue as a bare list or under a 'species' key and let any other shape fall through to a live count of zero, which would have reported llms.txt's figures as disagreeing with an empty catalogue -- a false report from one renamed key. The new branch concludes inconclusive there instead. What the check ASSERTS about the platform is unchanged: every stated species count in llms.txt must equal the live catalogue. It is stricter about what counts as a measurement and no weaker about what counts as a defect, so the pass it now produces is the same verification #55 documented the failure of.

The check definition moved on 2026-09-07 and the platform did not break. It compared the published reward figure as a STRING against digit runs pulled out of the channel's answer. That matched while the figures were integers; when the programme became a flat 1000.0 per verified bug, str() gave '1000.0' and the extractor gives '1000', so a channel answering correctly with 'ET10' and '1000' was scored as unable to state its own reward range. Verified directly against the live endpoint before changing anything: the answer contains both. The comparison is numeric now. What the check ASSERTS is unchanged -- the support channel must be able to report a value it publishes at /api/v1/bounty/reward-tiers -- so the pass it now produces is the same verification #66 documented the failure of.

The check definition moved on 2026-09-07 and the platform did not regress. It read the inbox and judged the newest first-pass reply, which meant it could only ever judge evidence someone else had produced -- and this morning the newest reply predated their fix, so re-running would never have cleared the finding. It now sends its own question and matches the reply by metadata.in_reply_to, which is what rule 7 asks for: a measurement taken after the claim. A reply that does not arrive within the window is recorded as role=evidence rather than inconclusive, so their agent being slow cannot turn a verified row into OUR CHECK CANNOT TELL and owe a repair_check on a check that works. What it ASSERTS is unchanged -- the async half must cite sources like the sync half -- and it now measures both halves in the same run instead of asserting one of them from a docstring. The pass it produces is the same verification #67 and #69 documented the failure of, taken on evidence this run created.

title: The bounty programme's own reward totals disagree: stats records 36 awards and 36,000 ET10, while every hunter on the leaderboard shows total_earned 0.0

reason: Report #73 documents the original failure: on 2026-09-07 stats recorded 36 awards and 36,000 ET10 while every hunter on the leaderboard showed total_earned 0.0, and the leaderboard accounted for 21 valid reports against the 40 stats called valid. They answered by publishing meaning rather than by moving a figure -- total_earned_definition 'paid', per-entry total_awarded and total_paid, and valid_reports split into attributed (35) and unattributed (6). The check was written for the other outcome and could not see that fix, so it was repaired in 26e97d7 to hold each hunter's total_earned against the column the platform names as its definition, and the board's sum against valid_reports_attributed. Strictly stronger than the definition it replaces, and proven to still fail: withdrawing total_earned_definition brings the original finding straight back.

Repaired, not redefined. The check asked whether a report of ours appears on /leaderboard/bugs by looking for the first 45 characters of its title in the page text. The page embeds titles in JSON, so report #73 is published as 'The bounty programme\u0027s own reward totals disagree' and the substring broke at character 21 -- the apostrophe. It called #73 absent from a tracker that was displaying it. The repair decodes \uXXXX and HTML entities on both sides and compares letters and digits only; the question it asks is unchanged, and it passes against the same page under the new definition. The original failure that opened this row is documented in report #61.
